name: UK energy price cap
summary: Ofgem cap £1,723 a year to 31 Dec; Cornwall Insight forecasts about £1,999 from January, about 16% higher
state: Ofgem's cap for 1 Oct to 31 Dec 2026 is £1,723 a year for a typical dual-fuel household, inside the £1,700–2,200 Watch band. Cornwall Insight's forecast, last updated 13 Nov and based on wholesale prices from 28 Sep, puts the January to March 2027 cap at about £1,999, roughly 16% higher (Cornwall Insight). That rise is above the 5% Watch line but below the 20% Alert line; Cornwall Insight's next update is due 18 Nov.
for_you: Households on standard variable tariffs are exposed to the January cap change, which Ofgem confirms in late November. Ofgem's website explains how the cap works and what help is available for those struggling with bills.
rubric_hit: Cap £1,723 in £1,700–2,200 Watch band; forecast rise ~16% ≥ 5% Watch line, < 20% Alert

sources.title: Cornwall Insight — Default tariff cap predictions and insights

why: The Ofgem cap sets bills for most UK households — a direct cost-of-living signal.
drivers: Wholesale gas and power prices, network costs, policy levies.

rubric.normal: Typical dual-fuel cap < £1,700/yr and next forecast change < +5%.
